conventions: lat = planetocentric latitude (deg, north positive); lon = east-positive longitude in -180..180 (deg). Where the source prints 0..360 E or a W longitude, the source value is kept in the quote and the conversion is stated in notes. Quotes were extracted from pages fetched in this session (WebFetch text extraction, or curl + pdftotext for PDFs / plain-text kernels). status=verified means the coordinate was read on a fetched primary or peer-reviewed page; unverified means Wikipedia-only, non-peer-reviewed, or not found.

apollo11_sun_elevation.source_title: NASA SP-4029 Apollo by the Numbers - Apollo 11 Summary (NASA History)
apollo11_sun_elevation.quote: "The planned launch window for Apollo 11 extended to 17:54:00 GMT to take advantage of a sun elevation angle" ... "on the lunar surface of 10.8°."
apollo11_sun_elevation.notes: CAVEAT: 10.8 deg is the PLANNED Sun elevation at the landing site that the launch window was built around, not a measured value at the actual touchdown instant. No fetched page states a Sun elevation exactly at 20:17:40 UT. Cross-check for validation: the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal 'Sun Angles' table (Brian W. Lawrence, https://apollojournals.org/alsj/sunangles.html) lists 'Landing: 102.75 GET' with no angle, then 'EVA Start: 109.00 GET, 14.0 deg.' and 'Finis: 111.75 GET, 15.4 deg.'. SP-4029 also says lunar sunlight incidence changed 'about 0.5° per hour'; 14.0 deg at 109.00 GET minus 6.25 h x ~0.5 deg/h gives roughly 10.9 deg at landing (my arithmetic, consistent with 10.8). A good validation target for the app is therefore ~10.8-11 deg at touchdown and 14.0 deg at 109:00 GET.
